import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.13

by D. I. Zaitsev

Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum
condition for normal subgroups?

Here a group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum (minimal) condition for normal
subgroups* if in every descending chain $N_1 \geq N_2 \geq \cdots$ of normal
subgroups of $G$ only finitely many of the indices $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ are
infinite. A group $G$ is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \cdots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
each of whose factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ satisfies the maximal condition or the
minimal condition on subgroups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.13»

/--
A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimal condition for normal subgroups* if for
every descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq \cdots$ of normal subgroups of $G$,
only finitely many of the indices $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ are infinite.

The index $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is `(N (i + 1)).relIndex (N i)`, which is `0`
exactly when the index is infinite.
-/
def WeakMinOnNormalSubgroups (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ i, (N i).Normal) → Antitone N →
    {i | (N (i + 1)).relIndex (N i) = 0}.Finite

/--
A group $G$ is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \cdots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$
each of whose factors $H_{i+1}/H_i$ satisfies either the maximal condition
(`WellFoundedGT`) or the minimal condition (`WellFoundedLT`) on subgroups.
-/
def IsMinimax (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    Monotone H ∧ H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ))) ∨
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)))

/-- The trivial group is minimax. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMinimax_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsMinimax G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, monotone_const, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- A group satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak minimal
condition for normal subgroups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMinOnNormalSubgroups.of_wellFoundedLT (G : Type*) [Group G]
    [WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)] : WeakMinOnNormalSubgroups G := by
  intro N _ hN
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := WellFoundedGT.monotone_chain_condition
    (α := (Subgroup G)ᵒᵈ) ⟨fun i => OrderDual.toDual (N i), fun _ _ h => hN h⟩
  refine (Set.finite_lt_nat n).subset fun m hm => ?_
  by_contra! h
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_lt] at h
  have h₁ : N m = N n := (hn m h).symm
  have h₂ : N (m + 1) = N n := (hn (m + 1) (by omega)).symm
  simp [Set.mem_setOf_eq, h₁, h₂, Subgroup.relIndex_self] at hm

/--
Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum
condition for normal subgroups?

That is: is every solvable group $G$ without non-trivial elements of finite
order that satisfies the weak minimal condition for normal subgroups a minimax
group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.13» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [IsSolvable G], (∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) →
      WeakMinOnNormalSubgroups G → IsMinimax G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.13»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group satisfies the maximum condition on subgroups if it has no infinite
strictly ascending chain of subgroups. -/
def SatisfiesMaxCondition : Prop :=
  WellFounded ((· > ·) : Subgroup G → Subgroup G → Prop)

/-- A group satisfies the minimum condition on subgroups if it has no infinite
strictly descending chain of subgroups. -/
def SatisfiesMinCondition : Prop :=
  WellFounded ((· < ·) : Subgroup G → Subgroup G → Prop)

/-- A group satisfies the weak minimum condition for normal subgroups if, for
every descending chain $G_0 \geq G_1 \geq \cdots$ of normal subgroups, the
index $[G_n:G_{n+1}]$ is finite for all but finitely many $n$. -/
def SatisfiesWeakMinNormalCondition : Prop :=
  ∀ series : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ n, (series n).Normal) → Antitone series →
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, (series (n + 1)).subgroupOf (series n) |>.FiniteIndex

/-- A group is minimax if it has a finite subnormal series from the whole group
to the trivial subgroup such that every factor satisfies either the maximum or
the minimum condition on subgroups. -/
def IsMinimax : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (series : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    Antitone series ∧ series 0 = ⊤ ∧ series (Fin.last n) = ⊥ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n,
        ∃ hnormal : ((series i.succ).subgroupOf (series i.castSucc)).Normal,
          letI := hnormal
          SatisfiesMaxCondition (series i.castSucc ⧸
              (series i.succ).subgroupOf (series i.castSucc)) ∨
            SatisfiesMinCondition (series i.castSucc ⧸
              (series i.succ).subgroupOf (series i.castSucc))

/--
Is every solvable torsion-free group that satisfies the weak minimum condition
for normal subgroups a minimax group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.13» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [IsSolvable G] [IsMulTorsionFree G],
      SatisfiesWeakMinNormalCondition G → IsMinimax G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.13»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.13

by D. I. Zaitsev

Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum condition for
normal subgroups?

Here a group is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series each of whose factors
satisfies either the maximal condition (Max) or the minimal condition (Min) on subgroups,
and a group satisfies the *weak minimum (minimal) condition for normal subgroups* if in
every descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq N_2 \geq \dots$ of normal subgroups all but
finitely many of the indices $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ are finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.13»

/--
A group $G$ is a *minimax group* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
each of whose factors $G_{i+1} / G_i$ satisfies either the maximal condition or the
minimal condition on subgroups.

The maximal (resp. minimal) condition on subgroups of a group `Q` is stated as
`WellFoundedGT (Subgroup Q)` (resp. `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup Q)`), i.e. `Q` has no
infinite strictly ascending (resp. strictly descending) chain of subgroups.
-/
def IsMinimax (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        WellFoundedGT (Subgroup (↥(s i.succ) ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))) ∨
        WellFoundedLT (Subgroup (↥(s i.succ) ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)))

/-- A finite group is minimax. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMinimax.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsMinimax G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, ?_⟩
  simp only [Fin.forall_fin_one, Fin.castSucc_zero, Fin.succ_zero_eq_one, Matrix.cons_val_zero,
    Matrix.cons_val_one]
  exact ⟨bot_le, inferInstance, Or.inl inferInstance⟩

/--
A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimal condition for normal subgroups* if for every
descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq N_2 \geq \dots$ of normal subgroups of $G$, the
index $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is finite for all but finitely many $i$.
-/
def WeakMinNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ i, (N i).Normal) → Antitone N →
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ i ≥ k, (N (i + 1)).IsFiniteRelIndex (N i)

/-- A finite group satisfies the weak minimal condition for normal subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMinNormal.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : WeakMinNormal G :=
  fun _ _ _ => ⟨0, fun _ _ => ⟨Subgroup.FiniteIndex.index_ne_zero⟩⟩

/-- A group satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak minimal
condition for normal subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMinNormal.of_wellFoundedLT (G : Type*) [Group G] [WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)] :
    WeakMinNormal G := by
  intro N _ hN
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := WellFoundedGT.monotone_chain_condition (α := (Subgroup G)ᵒᵈ) ⟨N, hN⟩
  refine ⟨k, fun i hi => ⟨?_⟩⟩
  have h1 : N (i + 1) = N i := (hk (i + 1) (by omega)).symm.trans (hk i hi)
  rw [h1, Subgroup.relIndex_self]
  exact one_ne_zero

/--
Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum condition for
normal subgroups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.13» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsSolvable G → IsMulTorsionFree G → WeakMinNormal G →
      IsMinimax G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.13»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table and its notes (subnormal series for minimax; Min-n-∞ as 'all but finitely many indices finite') agree with the standard literature definitions and were followed.
modeling_decisions: 'Minimax' uses a *subnormal* series (each term normal in the next), per the standard definition (Baer; Robinson, A Course in the Theory of Groups; Zaitsev) and the decomposition table. This is not equivalent to requiring a *normal* series even for soluble torsion-free groups (e.g. BS(1,p) = Z[1/p] ⋊ Z is minimax but has no normal series with Max/Min factors), so the choice matters and the standard one was taken.

Max/Min on subgroups of a factor Q are stated as `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup Q)` / `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup Q)`; the factor is the quotient type `↥(s i.succ) ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)`, whose group structure comes from an existentially bound `Normal` instance.

Descending chains in `WeakMinNormal` are indexed by ℕ and required only to be antitone (non-strict); this is equivalent to the strictly-descending formulation, and 'all but finitely many indices finite' is stated as `∃ k, ∀ i ≥ k, finite index`.
'Torsion-free' is Mathlib's class `IsMulTorsionFree G` (the repo's Kaplansky.lean uses the same); for groups it is equivalent to 'no nontrivial element of finite order'.
Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files.
Three short `@[category API]` lemmas were added as sanity tests of the bespoke definitions: finite groups are minimax and satisfy WeakMinNormal; groups with Min on subgroups satisfy WeakMinNormal.
